test_screenplay.pdf: A cluttered A&R office. Gold records line the walls. On a battered turntable, 'Take On Me' by a-ha plays loudly -- that unmistakable synth riff filling the room.
DIANA (40s, sharp) stands at the window, back to us. Her assistant, FELIX (20s, nervous), hovers in the doorway.
The Nielsen rep is here. And... he brought lawyers.
Of course he did. Turn that off.
Felix crosses to the turntable and lifts the needle.
The spinning vinyl slows. The label reads: WEA International. A Coca-Cola can sits beside it, logo facing the lens.
Diana turns. On the wall behind her hangs Nighthawks by Edward Hopper, a large print in a thin black frame.
You know that song? Take On Me? I actually love that song. It reminds me why I got into this business.
The Nielsen rep -- his name is Harman. Marcus Harman.
The Marcus Harman? I thought he retired.
INT./EXT. DIANA'S CAR - MOVING - LATE AFTERNOON
Diana drives. Felix rides shotgun, scrolling his phone. They pass a brightly lit Nobu restaurant -- Diana glances at it.
He says the Coca-Cola deal is dead. They found out about the Pepsi placement last quarter. Now they're threatening to pull their entire catalog.
To be, or not to be -- that is the question. Shakespeare said that and it's still the only thing worth saying in a negotiation.
INT. LAW FIRM - CONFERENCE ROOM - NIGHT
A long glass table. MARCUS HARMAN (60s, silver-haired, the actual music industry executive) sits at one end.
Across from him, Diana. Between them, a stack of contracts. A framed poster of Guernica by Pablo Picasso dominates the far wall.
Your client Dr. James Holloway signed a personal guarantee. The debt is real.
Dr. Holloway disagrees. And frankly, so do I.
Then we'll let the courts decide. I've been doing this for forty years. I have never lost a contract dispute.
Diana walks to her car alone. Her footsteps echo. She stops at a concrete pillar. Leans against it. Closes her eyes.
She opens her eyes. Takes out her phone. Dials.
It's me. We need to talk about the Holloway situation. Meet me at Nobu. Twenty minutes.
A vinyl booth under a flickering strip light. Felix slides a Coca-Cola bottle across the Formica. Diana does not touch it.
Coca-Cola tastes like syrup and battery acid. It rots your teeth out of your head and they put a polar bear on the can so nobody notices. I wouldn't pour it down a drain.
She pushes the bottle to the far edge of the table.
Diana waits under the awning. Felix catches up, out of breath.
There's another way through this. Taylor Swift re-recorded her first six albums when she couldn't buy the masters back. Holloway could do exactly the same thing.
Taylor Swift had thirty million people waiting for her. Holloway has a lawyer and a mortgage.
messy_screenplay.pdf: Steam. A radio plays 'Take On Me'. SARAH scrubs a pan.
You brought him here? To my kitchen?
He asked for you by name.
She sets the pan down. Turns.
Then he can ask again tomorrow, and the answer will be the same one I gave him the first time.
Marcus follows her out. A Coca-Cola machine hums.
Sarah. The Holloway estate is real.
The logo, dead centre. She kicks it.
The lot is empty. Rain starts.
